subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: What public inbound timing contract should OpenClaw expose for Gateway receipt time?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but automation should not choose the field name, timestamp type, or whether the value belongs in SDK context, prompt metadata, telemetry, or all of those surfaces.

options.title: Add generic gateway receipt metadata
options.body: Expose an additive `gatewayReceivedAt` or equivalent ISO/epoch field through the shared channel inbound context and agent-visible metadata, with tests across at least one queued and one direct inbound path.

options.title: Keep receipt time telemetry-only
options.body: Document that per-message Gateway receipt time is internal telemetry and close or re-scope this request to diagnostics rather than agent metadata.

options.title: Defer to channel-specific instrumentation
options.body: Track latency instrumentation only in affected channel issues such as LINE, Discord, or iMessage instead of adding a shared metadata contract now.

recommendation.title: Add generic gateway receipt metadata
recommendation.body: Expose an additive `gatewayReceivedAt` or equivalent ISO/epoch field through the shared channel inbound context and agent-visible metadata, with tests across at least one queued and one direct inbound path.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice affects the inbound metadata and prompt-cache boundary where steipete has the strongest feature-history signal.
